---
title: "Men vs Women"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/data-prep.R")

athlete_profiles <- beach_athletes |>
  filter(!is.na(age), !is.na(height)) |>
  mutate(
    medal_status = case_when(
      year >= 2020 ~ "Not reported in source",
      is.na(medal) ~ "No medal",
      TRUE ~ as.character(medal)
    ),
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", name, "</b>",
      "<br>Year: ", year,
      "<br>Event: ", gender,
      "<br>Age: ", age,
      "<br>Height: ", height, " cm",
      "<br>Medal status: ", medal_status
    )
  )
```

## Two events, one Olympic stage

Beach volleyball has featured men's and women's tournaments at every Games since its 1996 debut. Participation is measured in athlete-event records—two records for each competing pair—while podium results count each country-team once.

### Individual athlete profiles

Each point is a beach-volleyball athlete-event record. The age-height relationship is compared by event; shapes show medals only where the source records them.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes. Shows `r scales::comma(nrow(athlete_profiles))` of `r scales::comma(nrow(beach_athletes))` athlete-event records with reported height; medal status is unavailable in the source for 2020 and 2024."

profile_chart <- ggplot(
  athlete_profiles,
  aes(
    x = age,
    y = height,
    color = gender,
    shape = medal_status,
    text = hover_text
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8, alpha = 0.72) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Men = "#147f91", Women = "#c99837")) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(
      "Gold" = 17,
      "Silver" = 15,
      "Bronze" = 18,
      "No medal" = 16,
      "Not reported in source" = 4
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Height (cm)",
    color = "Event",
    shape = "Medal status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "#355260")
  )

plotly::ggplotly(profile_chart, tooltip = "text")
```

::: {.source-note}
Source: `olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes`. The chart plots **`r scales::comma(nrow(athlete_profiles))`** of **`r scales::comma(nrow(beach_athletes))`** athlete-event records with reported height; records without height are omitted. Medal status is not reported by this source for 2020 or 2024.
:::

### Participation through the years

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Beach volleyball participation by event and Games year. Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes; 756 athlete-event records across eight editions."

ggplot(
  beach_participation_by_year,
  aes(x = year, y = athlete_event_records, color = gender, group = gender)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Men = "#147f91", Women = "#c99837")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(beach_participation_by_year$year))) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Athlete-event records",
    color = "Event",
    caption = "Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes; beach volleyball identified from the event field."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#637780", hjust = 0)
  )
```

Recorded participation begins lower for women at the sport's debut: 36 athlete-event rows versus 48 for men in 1996. From 2000 through 2024, both events have 48 rows per Games in this dataset; these are athlete-event counts, not audience or popularity measures.

### Who reached the podium?

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Each point is one of 48 medal-winning country-teams. Panels compare men's and women's results by Olympic year; 2020 and 2024 podiums use official Olympic results."

gender_medal_chart <- beach_medals |>
  mutate(
    country = factor(country, levels = rev(country_medal_totals$country)),
    year = factor(year, levels = sort(unique(year)))
  ) |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = year,
      y = country,
      color = medal,
      text = paste(country, gender, year, medal, "team medal")
    )
  ) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.65),
    size = 2.8
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~gender, ncol = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(Gold = "#c99837", Silver = "#9caab5", Bronze = "#b87950"),
    breaks = c("Gold", "Silver", "Bronze")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Olympic year",
    y = "Medal-winning country",
    color = "Medal",
    caption = "Medals count country-teams, not athletes. 2020 and 2024 podiums use official Olympic results."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#10384a"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#637780", hjust = 0)
  )

plotly::ggplotly(gender_medal_chart, tooltip = "text")
```

::: {.source-note}
Sources: `olympicAthletes` for 1996–2016; official Olympic results for Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. The plot shows all **`r scales::comma(nrow(beach_medals))`** country-team medal results once each, not once per athlete.
:::

Across eight editions, each event awards 24 team medals. Brazil leads both tallies (8 women's and 6 men's medals), while the United States has 7 women's and 4 men's; Australia's three medals are all in the women's event.
